vehicleUpdates.summary: Five-seat used PHEV with related-trim evidence for three restraints including a rear-facing capsule. Check the centre seat and front clearance with your own restraints.

familyFit.summary: Related physical three-seat evidence is retained, but current Outlander manual guidance is disputed. This PHEV’s permitted mixed arrangement needs clarification; no family-fit score is assigned.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX pairs and three top tethers; centre tether is in the roof above the boot. ANCAP found a selected convertible and booster incompatible with the centre position.
familyFit.row3: No third row in this Aspire. Do not substitute seven-seat Exceed evidence.
familyFit.testedSeats: BabyDrive, April 2025 ES 20 kWh: three across including a rear-facing infant capsule. Full restraint models and positions are not named in the article.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Daily booster-buckle reach with three restraints was not assessed.
familyFit.access: Tester found the outboard ISOFIX and tether connections easy to use; centre tether connects through the boot. Fit your seats before judging daily loading.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear centre-console vents; two rows. Aspire has no sliding second row in the original 2023 test.

gaps: Your rear-facing seat, two other restraints, booster buckles and both adult front positions remain untested.
No exact Aspire mixed-restraint test found. The ES test supports a related cabin, not every seat combination.
Peak Australian AC/DC kW and EV-only purchased-energy consumption remain unverified; do not substitute mixed petrol/electric dashboard readings.
MY24 maker boot is 494 L; earlier Aspire tests quote 485 L. Confirm the actual build rather than treating grouped years as identical.
2021 ZL predecessor and original seven-seat Exceed are separate configurations.
inspection: Check the VIN against current official recall campaigns; this dataset is not a complete recall history.
Ask for proof that applicable rear-view camera software recall REC-005692 was completed.
Request a battery health report and demonstrate charging from your planned AC equipment.
Identify the 20 kWh specification from build/VIN, rather than registration year alone.
Australian MY 24 brochure specifies unleaded, minimum 91 RON recommended; select the matching fuel grade when editing petrol-cost assumptions.

The 7.2 L/100 km depleted figure is one roughly 50 km indicated test, not a repeatable lab or annual-cost guarantee. Do not buy grid electricity for its reported 19.6 kWh/100 km hybrid energy display; that includes energy generated by the petrol engine.
Try the rear-facing seat with the front seat set for each adult, then fit the centre restraint and check all buckle access.
Confirm the full Mitsubishi PHEV-dealer service history and remaining cover; several wear components have much shorter warranty terms.

ownershipUpdates.serviceInterval: ZM schedules: 12 months or 15,000 km, whichever first; severe-use work can be earlier. Confirm the exact model year and original purchase-date price cohort by VIN.
ownershipUpdates.serviceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$550/year for the grouped original 20 kWh Aspire at 15,000 km/year. Maker archive now verified: MY23 ten services A$5,090 (A$509/year); MY24 purchased by 30 November 2025 A$5,490 (A$549/year). Later purchase cohorts differ. This allowance is not the remaining-service total for a particular used car. Wear, severe-use extras and repairs are separate; obtain the VIN schedule.
warrantyCautions: Base cover is 5 years / 100,000 km. Eligible 10-year / 200,000-km extension requires every scheduled service from the first at an authorised Mitsubishi dealer, within the published 2-month / 2,000-km timing allowance. Missing one can end the extension while an unexpired base warranty remains; inspect the full history and original customer/use eligibility.

Drive-battery defects: 8 years/160,000 km for purchases after 1 October 2020. Capacity Care is separate: eligible MY22 onward batteries below 66% usable capacity; pre-MY22 Outlander is excluded. Confirm remaining cover and ownership details.

Capped servicing follows an eligible used vehicle until expiry; it does not restart at purchase. Prices depend on model year AND original purchase-date cohort. Government/rental and some business customers are excluded. The updated MY25 PHEV schedule for eligible purchases from 1 April 2026 is separately sourced; do not transfer it to earlier used purchases.

The full terms give shocks/struts, hoses, fuel injectors, LED/HID globes and other listed wear components only 12 months/20,000 km; the original 12 V battery has 12 months. Ten-year vehicle cover does not cover every part for ten years. Warranty transfers with ownership if its conditions remain satisfied; notify Mitsubishi of the transfer.

risks.title: Traction battery outside cover
risks.detail: No exact Australian fitted 20/22.7 kWh replacement quote was verified. A diagnostic battery report and warranty eligibility come before pack replacement; the displayed amount is a stress-case estimate, not a predicted failure.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$12,000–22,000 for a fitted replacement/aftermarket pack scenario, assuming labour and GST. Anchor: an Australian installer advertises an 18 kWh Outlander upgrade at A$14,600 incl GST; widen for newer 20/22.7 kWh packs and OEM sourcing. That upgrade is NOT verified compatible with this generation. No exact VIN quote or failure probability.
risks.warranty: Defect and Capacity Care eligibility differ; a qualifying maker remedy may be free.

risks.title: Cooling, transaxle and engine work
risks.detail: Inspect engine and motor cooling and transaxle leaks. Maker normal-use schedule specifies engine coolant first at 8 years/165,000 km and transaxle oil at 10 years/195,000 km; towing/rough-road use requires transaxle oil every 24 months/30,000 km. These are maintenance requirements, not common-failure claims.
risks.priceBasis: ESTIMATE — A$500–10,000 for ONE diagnosed cooling or major engine/transaxle event, not all systems together. Generic Australian cooling-fan work is A$240–610; a different 1.6T SUV engine is A$6,000–7,500 fitted. Wide PHEV planning allowance adds diagnosis, labour/GST and sourcing uncertainty; assembly replacement can exceed it. Routine servicing is separate.
risks.warranty: Scheduled fluids and wear are owner costs; an eligible manufacturing defect may be covered.

risks.title: Rear-camera software recall
risks.detail: Check campaign 010172 completion for affected 2021–2023 Outlander/PHEV VINs; camera images can be interrupted.
risks.priceBasis: A$0 for the official recall software remedy only, including dealer work; not a general camera-replacement quote.
risks.warranty: Free dealer software remedy for an affected VIN; unrelated camera hardware is a separate diagnosis.

energyEstimate.basis: ESTIMATE — battery-side kWh/100 km during electric driving for the 20 and 22.7 kWh Outlander PHEVs. Assume 85% usable pack energy (unverified), divide by each stated NEDC range (84/103 km), then allow about 10% road-use uplift: roughly 20.6–22.3. Round to 22 with 18–26 sensitivity. Not a measured consumption claim; apply charging loss once when buying electricity.

depletedEstimate.basis: ESTIMATE — 7.2 L/100 km planning point, with 5.5–8.5 sensitivity. Anchor is an indicated roughly 50 km depleted city/suburban/highway test of the original 20 kWh Australian Aspire. The exact old-car observation is separately recorded in its vehicle fact. Applying this to the later 22.7 kWh car is an unverified same-family analogue, not its manufacturer figure or a measured later-car result. Weighted 1.5/1.2 are not substituted.

outlander-phev-aspire-227.serviceBasis: MANUFACTURER PLAN — exact Australian MY25 Outlander 4x4 2.4L PHEV schedule for eligible purchases from 1 April 2026, matching the updated 22.7 kWh brochure designation. Ten normal-use visits at 12 months / 15,000 km cost A$377,449,399,499,399,899,399,899,499,899: A$5,718 over ten years / 150,000 km, or A$571.80/year averaged. The A$377–899 sensitivity is the lowest/highest individual visit, not uncertainty in the published caps. This is not a promise every used VIN has all ten visits remaining. Covered scheduled parts, labour, oils and fluids only; wear, missed-service catch-up, severe-use extras and repairs are additional. Confirm purchase-date eligibility and GST treatment on the dealer invoice.

reviewUpdates.scope: No clean configuration-specific owner aggregate verified. Public ZM PHEV page displays 4.7/5 from four reviews, including an explicit 2021 GSR owner from the previous generation.
reviewUpdates.summary: The published 4.7/5 is retained here as context, but excluded from the scored owner rating because the four-review sample mixes generations. The updated 22.7 kWh car has no isolated subset.
positiveThemes: Smooth electric acceleration and quiet running
Sliding second row and space for family use
Petrol backup alongside regular electric driving
negativeThemes: Some cabin noise and startup/infotainment annoyances
Third row described by one owner as occasional-use space
Economy varies with charging and driving mode

Youi A$785–1,531 covers mixed Outlander years/powertrains; it is not a PHEV quote. A$1,300–2,900 bounds are analyst assumptions. Replace with your address, driver, excess and insured-value quote; CTP is separate in rego.

tyreUpdates.basis: Budget aftermarket anchor: Radar Dimax R8+ 105Y XL, A$289 each × 4 = A$1,156 fitted. Preserves or exceeds previous replacement-reference ratings; Ordinary JAX advertised price includes fitting, balancing, tubeless valves, disposal, selected-store delivery and GST; no temporary multi-buy discount used. Store stock and Brisbane availability are unconfirmed. Life is a common 40,000 km planning assumption (25,000–60,000 km sensitivity), not a measured model or tyre average. Wear varies with tyre choice, driving, maintenance and vehicle; model-specific replacement averages were not verified. Annual allowance = set budget × annual km ÷ 40,000, rounded to A$10. Age/damage can require earlier replacement. Alignment is additional; actual placard, wheel package and local fitted quote must be checked. Matching size/load/speed does not establish equal braking, efficiency or durability.

repairReserveUpdates.basis: Used PHEV has petrol and electric systems. Ten-year vehicle cover depends on service eligibility; battery cover is separate. Verify the actual service history and exclusions. Analyst savings allowance, not an observed average repair bill. Rounded assumptions use age, cover and component costs. Deep audit found no credible Australian annual fault-rate / out-of-pocket dataset for these exact Aspires. Keep this low-confidence buffer; conditional dealer-service cover and short-cover wear parts matter more than anecdote counts.

items.finding: Two distinct used QLD asks remain A$44,990–48,500 drive-away, 7,815–43,477 km; median A$46,745. Updated new NSW/TAS asks A$67,420–72,490, median A$69,955; no QLD drive-away quote. Thin samples and interstate charges remain material.

Maker PDFs verify 20 / 22.7 kWh, 84 / 103 km ADR/NEDC, Type 2 / CHAdeMO, 91 RON, and charging times. Original depleted 7.2 L/100 km is a short indicated Aspire test. Neither exact EV-only purchased-energy use nor peak AU charging kW was established; retain labelled estimates.

Related older ES physical mixed fit is documented, but BabyDrive now reports conflicting Mitsubishi explanations of a left/centre occupancy caution. Exact Australian PHEV manual applicability and permitted installations remain unresolved. Updated 22.7 kWh mixed fit is also unverified. Family-fit scores are withheld; this is not a blanket claim that all Outlanders prohibit three seats. ANCAP selected-centre restraint failures and no row-three tether fallback remain relevant.

Base 5 years/100,000 km, conditional extension to 10 years/200,000 km, transfers with eligible service history. Battery defects and 66% capacity remedy have separate 8-year/160,000-km terms. Several wear components only 12 months/20,000 km; 12 V battery 12 months.

12 months/15,000 km. Exact maker ten-visit totals: MY23 A$5,090; MY24 purchased by 30 November 2025 A$5,490; updated MY25 bought from 1 April 2026 A$5,718. Keep grouped original A$550/year estimate and updated A$571.80 override. Severe-use transaxle fluids can add work.

No exact household or Aspire quote found. A$1,900/year remains a low-confidence HEV/PHEV proxy, not measured PHEV premium. Youi’s broader Outlander band cannot replace it without matching driver, variant and insured value.

Budget aftermarket audit, 18 October 2026. 255/45R20 105Y XL replacement reference: A$1,156 for four fitted. Common 40,000 km life is an illustrative assumption, not model-specific wear evidence. Prices and annual savings are estimates; check the real placard and local fitted quote.

No empirical AU annual repair average or exact fitted 20/22.7 kWh battery quote found. Keep A$850 original / A$650 updated savings buffers low confidence. Recall 010172 is free for affected VINs; 010175 steering campaign is Exceed/Exceed Tourer, not an Aspire-wide fault. Do not transfer old-generation or overseas problems.

Public ZM PHEV 4.7/5 from four reviews includes an explicit pre-ZM 2021 owner, so clean owner rating is unavailable and excluded from scoring. Exact original Aspire professional review remains 7.5/10; current Exceed qualitative review is related trim, not exact Aspire.

Both brochures list 1,600 kg braked / 160 kg towball, tyre repair kit and separate ANCAP applicability. Four-cylinder QLD rego plus Class 1 CTP guide A$864.50–880.50/year (midpoint A$872.50); hybrid duty A$2 per A$100 up to A$100,000. Resale and household risk remain estimates.
